PHMY 600.description: The first course in the personal and professional development series imparts to the student pharmacist the knowledge, skills, abilities, behaviors, and attitudes necessary to provide patient education and demonstrate self-awareness and professionalism.
PHMY 600.subject: PHMY
PHMY 600.title: Personal and Professional Development for Student Pharmacists I

PHMY 601.description: The second course in the personal and professional development series imparts to the student pharmacist the knowledge, skills, abilities, behaviors, and attitudes necessary to provide patient education; patient and professional advocacy; collaborative and inclusive patient care; and to demonstrate self-awareness and professionalism.
PHMY 601.subject: PHMY
PHMY 601.title: Personal and Professional Development for Student Pharmacists II

PHMY 602.description: An introduction to the basic principles and concepts of physiology, pathophysiology and pharmacology.
PHMY 602.subject: PHMY
PHMY 602.title: Foundations of Pathophysiology and Pharmacology I

PHMY 603.description: This is the second course in the series addressing the basic principles and concepts of physiology, pathophysiology and pharmacology.
PHMY 603.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PHMY 602; first professional year standing.
PHMY 603.subject: PHMY
PHMY 603.title: Foundations of Pathophysiology and Pharmacology II

PHMY 607.description: A study of the physiochemical principles of the formulation, preparation, properties, and performance of the pharmaceutical dosage forms. Clinical application of the various dosage forms in patient care will be discussed.
PHMY 607.subject: PHMY
PHMY 607.title: Dosage Forms and Drug Delivery Systems

PHMY 610.description: Introduction to the role of immunology in human disease and the properties, resistance patterns, diagnostic tools and clinical pearls of common (and not so common) bacterial, viral, fungal and parasitic infectious agents.
PHMY 610.subject: PHMY
PHMY 610.title: Microbiology/Immunology

PHMY 615.description: The course covers the molecular and biochemical basis of human biology and physiology. The properties and functions of biological molecules and biochemical pathways are covered. Emphasis is placed on the molecular basis of human physiology, causes of human diseases and how drugs produce biological effects.
PHMY 615.subject: PHMY
PHMY 615.title: Pharmaceutical Biochemistry

PHMY 618.description: The course focuses on nucleic acids as the core theme and examines the pathways used for transmission and expression of genetic information. Topics also include the cell cycle (mitosis) and gametogenesis (meiosis). Students will learn to apply knowledge of human genetic variation that influences drug therapy decision making. Recombinant DNA technology is covered as applied to the study of human health such as personalized medicine, genetic testing, stem cell therapy, gene therapy, RNA silencing, and production of biopharmaceuticals. Antibodies are discussed from the perspective of their use in diagnostic testing, as well as the utilization of antibodies as therapeutics.
PHMY 618.subject: PHMY
PHMY 618.title: Genomics, Pharmacogenomics, and Personalized Medicine

PHMY 621.description: This course includes an introduction to the basic principles and concepts of medicinal chemistry and pharmacogenomics including the relationships of molecular structure to drug absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion. The chemical rationale for drug therapeutic actions and side effects as well as the pharmacogenomics basis for individualized drug therapy is discussed.
PHMY 621.subject: PHMY
PHMY 621.title: Foundations of Medicinal Chemistry I

PHMY 624.description: In an integrated approach to first year pharmacy education, Foundations in Medicinal Chemistry II will serve as a complementary course to PHMY 618 Genomics, Pharmacogenomics, and Personalized Medicine. We will utilize the principles and concepts learned in general and organic chemistry and PHMY621 to introduce the general molecular properties of pharmaceutical agents. The course will consist of a survey of the medicinal chemistry of the remaining major drug classes not covered in PHMY 621 . Pharmacogenomic information will be emphasized where known and applicable to help explain variations in both therapeutic and side effects due to receptor structure, metabolism and/or other pharmacokinetic properties.
PHMY 624.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PHMY 621; first professional year standing.
PHMY 624.subject: PHMY
PHMY 624.title: Foundations of Medicinal Chemistry II

PHMY 650.description: Introduction to the professional issues relevant to the practice of pharmacy.
PHMY 650.subject: PHMY
PHMY 650.title: Introduction to Pharmacy Practice

PHMY 651.description: This course introduces professional issues relevant to the practice of pharmacy including access and utilization of drug information resources.
PHMY 651.subject: PHMY
PHMY 651.title: Foundations of Pharmacy Practice

PHMY 656.description: This course develops the mathematic skills and knowledge required in various pharmacy practice settings. Problem solving skills will be developed as students become proficient in basic math skills used to solve pharmacy calculations based word problems which are commonly seen in a variety of practice settings, including community, compounding, hospital, and nuclear pharmacy.
PHMY 656.subject: PHMY
PHMY 656.title: Pharmacy Calculations

PHMY 657.description: A thorough knowledge of medical terminology is an essential building block in pharmacy education. This web-based course will aid the student in learning the language and terminology used in other pharmacy courses and all areas of pharmacy practice.
PHMY 657.subject: PHMY
PHMY 657.title: Medical Terminology

PHMY 661.description: Case-based discussions that integrate and demonstrate applicability of other course material.
PHMY 661.subject: PHMY
PHMY 661.title: Clinical Applications II

PHMY 662.description: This course introduces basic patient care fundamentals such as interpreting laboratory values, patient care planning processes, and clinical documentation. The course integrates basic sciences concepts, such as pharmacogenomics, with patient care. It also affords the student opportunities to practice medical literature searches, literature evaluation, and to recognize the social determinants of health in order to diminish disparities and inequities in access to quality care.
PHMY 662.subject: PHMY
PHMY 662.title: Patient Care Fundamentals

PHMY 670.description: Interactive laboratory session designed to provide students with a thorough understanding of community pharmacy practice skills, to include the knowledge of prescription and drug order processing necessary to function in community pharmacy practice at a basic level.
PHMY 670.subject: PHMY
PHMY 670.title: Pharmacy Skill Lab II: Introduction to Community Pharmacy

PHMY 671.description: The art, science and technology of pharmacy compounding.
PHMY 671.subject: PHMY
PHMY 671.title: Pharmacy Skills Lab I: Compounding and Applied Pharmaceutics

PHMY 680.description: Basic principles of access and utilization of drug information resources.
PHMY 680.subject: PHMY
PHMY 680.title: Introduction to Drug Information

PHMY 690.description: The course goal is to lay the foundations for beginning health professions students to understand the complexities of the health care system and the role of interprofessional collaboration to improve the system. Through an interprofessional context, students will explore the art and science of teamwork and communication skills, cultural competency, ethical issues, healthcare disparities and social determinants of health, as well as develop ways to improve healthcare systems and patient safety.
PHMY 690.subject: PHMY
PHMY 690.title: Transforming Healthcare

PHMY 699.description: Introduction to the practice of the pharmacy in the community pharmacy setting. Forty hours of directed experience per week for four weeks.
PHMY 699.subject: PHMY
PHMY 699.title: Introductory Community Practice Pharmacy Experience

PHMY 700.description: The third course in the personal and professional development series which imparts to the student pharmacist the knowledge, skills, abilities, behaviors, and attitudes necessary to provide patient education and demonstrate self-awareness and professionalism.
PHMY 700.subject: PHMY
PHMY 700.title: Personal and Professional Development for Student Pharmacists III

PHMY 701.description: The fourth course in the personal and professional development series imparts to the student pharmacist the knowledge, skills, abilities, behaviors, and attitudes necessary to provide patient education; patient and professional advocacy; collaborative and inclusive patient care; and to demonstrate self-awareness and professionalism.
PHMY 701.subject: PHMY
PHMY 701.title: Personal and Professional Development for Student Pharmacists IV

PHMY 710.description: Study of the pharmacokinetics of drug absorption, distribution, and elimination (metabolism and excretion). Introductory application of pharmacokinetics to drug interactions and dosage regimen design and adjustment, selected disease states and special populations.
PHMY 710.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PHMY 607; second professional year standing.
PHMY 710.subject: PHMY
PHMY 710.title: Biopharmaceutics and Pharmacokinetics

PHMY 716.description: An individualized program of study or research arranged by consultation between student and faculty member. Credit is variable and the course may be repeated for credit.
PHMY 716.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: second or third professional year standing or in fulfillment of graduate program requirement or honors thesis.
PHMY 716.subject: PHMY
PHMY 716.title: Special Project, Dept. of Pharmaceutical Biomedical Sciences

PHMY 717.description: An overview of basic concepts in cancer epidemiology, genetics, and biology, and the therapeutic approaches utilized in the prevention and treatment of cancer.
PHMY 717.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: second or third professional year standing.
PHMY 717.subject: PHMY
PHMY 717.title: Cancer: Causes, Treatment, and Prevention

PHMY 722.description: The first course in a series that applies pathophysiology and pharmacology principles introduced in the foundations courses in the first year in an organ-based approach. The course is designed to integrate organ system pathophysiology and pharmacology with pharmacotherapy.
PHMY 722.subject: PHMY
PHMY 722.title: Pathophysiologyand Pharmacology I

PHMY 723.description: The second course in a series that applies pathophysiology and pharmacology concepts introduced in the foundations courses in the first year in an organ-based approach. The course is designed to integrate organ system pathophysiology and pharmacology with pharmacotherapy.
PHMY 723.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PHMY 722; second professional year standing.
PHMY 723.subject: PHMY
PHMY 723.title: Pathophysiology and Pharmacology II

PHMY 750.description: A review of indications, contraindications, and cautions involved with the recommendation and dispensing of nonprescription (OTC) drug items and complementary medicines.
PHMY 750.subject: PHMY
PHMY 750.title: Self-Care and Complementary Medicines

PHMY 751.description: This course develops critical thinking skills required for pharmacy practice through case-based discussions and care plan development designed to integrate and demonstrate applicability of current coursework and previous knowledge gained from prior course material in patient centered care.
PHMY 751.subject: PHMY
PHMY 751.title: Patient Care Applications I

PHMY 752.description: This course further develops critical thinking skills required for pharmacy practice through case-based discussions and care plan development designed to integrate and demonstrate applicability of current coursework and previous knowledge gained from prior course material in patient centered care.
PHMY 752.subject: PHMY
PHMY 752.title: Patient Care Applications II

PHMY 756.description: This course will introduce students to the principles of solid organ transplantation (SOT) and the role of a pharmacist in the continuum of care for transplant recipients through case-based learning and exposure to primary literature. Students will learn indications, common disease processes, and complications associated with kidney, pancreas, liver, lung, and heart transplantation in addition to the management of population-specific immunosuppression pharmacotherapy regimens.
PHMY 756.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: second or third professional year standing.
PHMY 756.subject: PHMY
PHMY 756.title: Clinical Immunology and Transplant

PHMY 757.description: An individualized program of study or research arranged by consultation between student and faculty member. Credit is variable and the course may be repeated for credit.
PHMY 757.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: second or third professional year standing or in fulfillment of graduate program requirement or honors thesis.
PHMY 757.subject: PHMY
PHMY 757.title: Special Project, Dept of Pharmacy and Outcome Sciences

PHMY 760.description: Case-based discussions that integrate and demonstrate applicability of other course material in patient care.
PHMY 760.subject: PHMY
PHMY 760.title: Clinical Applications III

PHMY 761.description: Case-based discussions that integrate and demonstrate applicability of other course material in patient care.
PHMY 761.subject: PHMY
PHMY 761.title: Clinical Applications IV

PHMY 762.description: This course is designed to teach students the leadership skills needed to influence people and organizations in an effort to create positive change within the practice of pharmacy.
PHMY 762.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: second or third professional year standing.
PHMY 762.subject: PHMY
PHMY 762.title: Creating Pharmacy Leaders

PHMY 763.description: The course will emphasize aspects of pharmacy career development, to include understanding of the role of a professional, strategies in dealing with various types of patients, development of professional presentations, and familiarity with career pathways in pharmacy.
PHMY 763.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: second or third professional year standing.
PHMY 763.subject: PHMY
PHMY 763.title: Introduction to Pharmacy Pathways and Careers

PHMY 764.description: This course is designed to provide the health care practitioner with the knowledge and skills to manage their personal finances in an effective manner. After successfully completing this course, the student will be able to understand the process for making personal financial decisions; establish personal financial goals; evaluate the factors that influence personal financial planning; and apply strategies for attaining personal financial goals.
PHMY 764.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: second or third professional year standing.
PHMY 764.subject: PHMY
PHMY 764.title: Personal Finance

PHMY 765.description: This course will provide students with an overview of the pharmaceutical industry with an emphasis on the drug development process, clinical research, business development, regulatory affairs, and marketing.
PHMY 765.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: second or third year professional year standing.
PHMY 765.subject: PHMY
PHMY 765.title: Introduction to Pharmaceutical Industry

PHMY 766.description: This course is designed to expose the student to a wide variety of herbal medicines and dietary supplements. Discussions will also include regulation of herbal supplements, evaluation of the alternative medicine literature, and disease-directed discussions with case studies.
PHMY 766.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: second or third professional year standing.
PHMY 766.subject: PHMY
PHMY 766.title: Alternative Medicine

PHMY 767.description: This course will teach students to consider social determinants of health when interacting with patients. Students will characterize the role of various healthcare professions in reducing health-disparities and -inequities. Students will learn to communicate with and advocate for patients through interactions with content experts and development of interview-style podcasts.
PHMY 767.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: second or third professional year standing.
PHMY 767.subject: PHMY
PHMY 767.title: Off the SCRIPT: Conversations in Health Care

PHMY 768.description: This elective course provides a variety of experiences for students to expand their understanding of healthcare disparities, rural healthcare and begin professional networking in a rural area of South Carolina. Students will develop and employ entrepreneurship skills to design a career plan for a pharmacist in a rural community. Students will develop and employ leadership skills to design an initiative to advance healthcare within a rural community. Students will also develop and employ research skills to design a proposal for evaluating their initiative to advance healthcare within a rural community.
PHMY 768.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: Second or third professional year standing.
PHMY 768.subject: PHMY
PHMY 768.title: Advancing Rural/Underserved Care and Health

PHMY 769.description: This course offers valuable insights into hormonal changes that nearly all female patients will experience over the life span along with appropriate clinical utilization of drug therapy in this population. This course covers hormonal physiology, clinical presentations of imbalance, and therapeutic management approaches during key hormonal transitions. The main focus on this course will be related to peri-menopause, menopause, and post-menopause but discussion of issues impacting younger women with hormonal imbalance will be covered.
PHMY 769.subject: PHMY
PHMY 769.title: Women’s Health Age-Related Hormone Therapy

PHMY 771.description: Provide students with an advanced knowledge of prescription and drug order processing, and assist them in the development of appropriate skills necessary for provision of pharmaceutical care to patients in the community setting, through the use of medication profiles, patient counseling, personal interviews, and appropriate prescription and non-prescription drug information.
PHMY 771.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PHMY 670; third professional year standing.
PHMY 771.subject: PHMY
PHMY 771.title: Pharmacy Skills Lab V: Applied Community Pharmacy

PHMY 772.description: This course is the first in a 4-semester sequence of courses providing an organ-based approach to pharmaceutical care and disease management. Students will learn about disease prevention and health promotion, as well as the drug and non-drug therapy of acute and chronic diseases seen in both hospitalized and ambulatory patients. Emphasis is placed on preventing, identifying, and solving drug-related problems. This course is coordinated with Pathophysiology and Pharmacology I.
PHMY 772.subject: PHMY
PHMY 772.title: Pharmacotherapy I

PHMY 773.description: This course is the second in a 4-semester sequence of courses providing a systems-based approach to pharmaceutical care and disease management. Students will learn about disease prevention and health promotion, as well as the drug and non-drug therapy of acute and chronic diseases seen in both hospitalized and ambulatory patients. Emphasis is placed on preventing, identifying, and solving drug-related problems. This course is coordinated with Pathophysiology and Pharmacology II.
PHMY 773.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PHMY 772; second professional year standing.
PHMY 773.subject: PHMY
PHMY 773.title: Pharmacotherapy II

PHMY 774.description: This class will focus on enabling students to become advocates for the pharmacy profession through review of current legislation that affects pharmacists and healthcare, as well as determining the impact of legislation on the profession. Students will learn how to affect legislation through contact with their representatives and through collaboration with pharmacy organizations. Concepts for providing to their representatives a concise review of the effect of legislation will also be reviewed.
PHMY 774.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: second or third professional year standing.
PHMY 774.subject: PHMY
PHMY 774.title: Pharmacy Political Advocacy

PHMY 776.description: This course will prepare students to develop and implement a pharmaceutical a pharmaceutical care service into a community pharmacy setting. The focus will be on designing a Medication Therapy Management service; however other clinical pharmacy services will be discussed. Students will apply basic principles of small business administration and development to the creation of a pharmacy service. Students will participate in interactive lectures, written assignments, and formal presentations.
PHMY 776.subject: PHMY
PHMY 776.title: Developing a Medication Therapy Management Service

PHMY 779.description: This elective focuses on developing critical thinking, problem solving, and communication skills by incorporating principles of self-management covered in Self-care and Complementary Medicines ( PHMY 750 ) into evidence-based case discussions and presentations.
PHMY 779.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: second or third professional standing.
PHMY 779.subject: PHMY
PHMY 779.title: Advanced Self-Care

PHMY 780.description: Common statistical methods and study designs used in pharmacoepidemiology and outcomes research, as well as to issues related to the measurement, analysis, and interpretation of results of clinical trials and outcomes studies.
PHMY 780.subject: PHMY
PHMY 780.title: Outcomes Design and Assessment

PHMY 784.description: This course is designed to prepare students for and promote post-graduate training, with an emphasis on residency training, but also including PhD and fellowship training. All elements of preparation for post-graduate training will be covered; the class will provide information related to various types of research, discuss the ethical considerations related to research and provide the opportunity to develop and present a research protocol.
PHMY 784.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: second or third professional year standing.
PHMY 784.subject: PHMY
PHMY 784.title: Post-graduate and Research Training

PHMY 785.description: Didactic lectures and discussions involving content from relevant textbooks and research literature on the principles of pharmacoepidemiology, research design, and statistical techniques.
PHMY 785.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: Second or third professional year standing.
PHMY 785.subject: PHMY
PHMY 785.title: Principles of Pharmacoepidemiology

PHMY 786.description: This challenging course is designed to provide the student with increased exposure to disease states, medication issues, and clinical decision-making skills specific to the pediatric population. Pediatrics is an integral component to most pharmacy careers, and gaining a greater understanding of the patient population’s challenges and nuances is necessary to become a confident and well-rounded practitioner. This elective also seeds to provide exposure to the pediatric pharmacy community, including experts in the subspecialty areas and organizations.
PHMY 786.subject: PHMY
PHMY 786.title: Pediatric Pharmacotherapy

PHMY 788.description: This course introduces health professions students to concepts in community and public health focusing on childhood obesity. The course is in collaboration with the Junior Doctors of Health (JDOH) program. JDOH is an interprofessional service-learning program that works with children in low-income schools with the aim of long term prevention of childhood obesity. During the course, students will lead education and interactive sessions that are part of the JDOH curriculum to promote healthy diet and physical activity behaviors. Students from public health, social work, and pharmacy will participate in didactic class sessions together then will provide education regarding the prevention of childhood obesity as interprofessional teams to elementary students in local schools. Teams will then develop presentations regarding their experiences to present during the final class session.
PHMY 788.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: second or third professional year standing.
PHMY 788.subject: PHMY
PHMY 788.title: Interprofessional Prevention of Childhood Obesity

PHMY 790.description: Introduction to Health-Systems Pharmacy is designed to develop essential pharmacy practice skills within a health-system setting. This course provides students with foundational knowledge and hands-on experience in key areas of health-system pharmacy, including pharmacy operations, sterile compounding, and dispensing processes.
PHMY 790.subject: PHMY
PHMY 790.title: Pharmacy Skills Lab III: Introduction to Health-Systems Pharmacy

PHMY 791.description: Applied Health-Systems Pharmacy builds upon foundational skills from Introduction to Health-Systems Pharmacy, further preparing students for roles within diverse health-system settings. This course expands students’ understanding of advanced pharmacy operations, introducing a range of concepts and practices integral to effective health-systems pharmacy.
PHMY 791.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PHMY 790; second professional year standing.
PHMY 791.subject: PHMY
PHMY 791.title: Pharmacy Skills Lab IV: Applied Health-Systems Pharmacy

PHMY 792.description: This course will build upon the knowledge acquired in the first professional year courses Dosage Forms/Drug Delivery Systems and Compounding/Applied Pharmaceutics lab. The course will provide emphasis on practical application in the evaluation of unique dosage forms, pharmacotherapy, and special pharmaceutical needs of various patient populations. This course is self-paced and delivered in an online format utilizing prerecorded lectures.
PHMY 792.subject: PHMY
PHMY 792.title: Advanced Pharmacy Compounding I

PHMY 793.description: This course is an elective course that provides additional insight and understanding into a variety of pharmacy compounding topics, which include nutrient depletion, drug-induced nutrient depletion, metabolic demands of athletes, men’s health, and family medicine. This course is self-paced and delivered in an online format utilizing prerecorded lectures.
PHMY 793.subject: PHMY
PHMY 793.title: Advanced Topics in Pharmacy Compounding II

PHMY 794.description: This course introduces students to the principles and practices of entrepreneurship within the pharmacy profession. Emphasis is placed on developing the skills and mindset necessary to identify opportunities, innovate, and create value in healthcare settings. Through guided application of design thinking and business modeling, students will work to address a real-world challenge in pharmacy practice and present a formal business pitch to a panel.
PHMY 794.subject: PHMY
PHMY 794.title: Pharmacist Entrepreneurship

PHMY 798.description: Introduction to the practice of the pharmacy in the institutional setting. Forty hours of directed experience per week for four weeks.
PHMY 798.subject: PHMY
PHMY 798.title: Introductory Institutional Practice Pharmacy Experience

PHMY 800.description: The fifth course in the personal and professional development series which imparts to the student pharmacist the knowledge, skills, abilities, behaviors, and attitudes necessary to provide patient education and demonstrate self-awareness and professionalism.
PHMY 800.subject: PHMY
PHMY 800.title: Personal and Professional Development for Student Pharmacists V

PHMY 801.description: The final course in the personal and professional development series which imparts to the student pharmacist the knowledge, skills, abilities, behaviors, and attitudes necessary to demonstrate patient education; patient and professional advocacy, collaborative and inclusive patient care; leadership; innovation and entrepreneurship; self-awareness and professionalism.
PHMY 801.subject: PHMY
PHMY 801.title: Personal and Professional Development for Student Pharmacists VI

PHMY 822.description: This is the third in a 4-semester sequence of courses aimed at integrating the discussion of specific disease states and the mechanism of action of the pharmacologic agents used to treat those disease states. This knowledge will be integrated, utilized and applied in a parallel sequence of courses in Pharmacotherapy using an organ-system based approach emphasizing pharmaceutical care and disease management.
PHMY 822.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PHMY 722, PHMY 723; third year professional standing.
PHMY 822.subject: PHMY
PHMY 822.title: Pathophysiology and Pharmacology III

PHMY 823.description: This is the fourth in a 4-semester sequence of courses aimed at integrating the discussion of specific disease states and the mechanism of action of the pharmacologic agents used to treat those disease states. This knowledge will be integrated, utilized an applied in a parallel sequence of courses in Pharmacotherapy using an organ-system based approach emphasizing pharmaceutical care and disease management.
PHMY 823.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PHMY 822; third year professional standing.
PHMY 823.subject: PHMY
PHMY 823.title: Pathophysiology and Pharmacology IV

PHMY 850.description: This course provides insight and understanding of the U.S. health care system and pharmacy's role within that system. Managerial skills and concepts are taught to allow pharmacists to maximize their contribution to this health care system and to the patients it serves.
PHMY 850.subject: PHMY
PHMY 850.title: Health Care Systems and Management

PHMY 851.description: A disease-oriented and organ-integrated approach to the care of patients with acute illnesses managed in the in-patient hospital setting. Students will learn common disease processes that affect the acutely ill hospitalized patient and the appropriate pharmacotherapy to treat these patients. This course focuses on developing critical thinking and problem solving skills, and integrating material from this course and previous courses in a case-based format.
PHMY 851.subject: PHMY
PHMY 851.title: Acute Care Therapeutics

PHMY 852.description: This course provides students with an in-depth understanding of the operational and financial aspects of starting, owning, and managing a community pharmacy. Students will gain knowledge and skills necessary to evaluate an existing pharmacy and look for opportunities to optimize workflow and operations. Learning opportunities will include on-site visits, meetings with pharmacy owners, and discussions within the course.
PHMY 852.subject: PHMY
PHMY 852.title: Owning and Managing an Independent Pharmacy

PHMY 855.description: Students will be exposed to the process of designing a research experiment from idea conception through manuscript submission, including protocol development, IRB approval, abstract submission, grant funding, and peer review. Students will also familiarize themselves with technology commonly used in data collection, analysis, and manuscript writing. Weekly opportunities to engage with accomplished health science researchers will allow the student to be exposed to numerous research designs. The overall goal of this course is to make the student prepared to step in and work in a faculty mentored research study.
PHMY 855.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: second or third professional year standing.
PHMY 855.subject: PHMY
PHMY 855.title: The What, Why, and How of Health Sciences Research

PHMY 856.description: This course is designed to instruct students on the proper approach to critical evaluation of the medical literature. An evidence based approach to patient care hinges on the medical team’s ability to utilize the most current literature available. Students will learn the keys to critiquing the medical literature, including basic statistical and analytical concepts, in an open forum style, with application of literature information to clinical scenarios.
PHMY 856.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: second or third professional year standing.
PHMY 856.subject: PHMY
PHMY 856.title: Evidence Based Medicine

PHMY 857.description: This course provides a practical look at independent community pharmacy, including the many aspects involved in starting, owning and running a pharmacy business. Sessions will focus on critically appraising the unique aspects of independent pharmacy ownership/management or sustainable pharmacy services. Learning opportunities will include management skill development and on-site visits.
PHMY 857.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: second or third professional year standing.
PHMY 857.subject: PHMY
PHMY 857.title: Community Pharmacy Practice and Operations

PHMY 858.description: This course is designed to prepare students to appropriately recognize, predict, assess, and manage drug interactions that are encountered in pharmacy practice.
PHMY 858.subject: PHMY
PHMY 858.title: Drug Interactions

PHMY 859.description: This course is designed to provide students with exposure to clinical research. The demand for pharmacist researchers in a variety of settings continues to increase, and clinical pharmacists are often called upon to engage in some research activities. Residency training provides practical application of research; however, most residents lack an in-depth exposure to the varied aspects of research prior to graduation. This class will provide students with information related to various types of research, discuss the ethical considerations related to clinical research, and provide students with the opportunity to develop and present a clinical research protocol. This course will help prepare students for post-graduate (residency, fellowship, or PhD) research endeavors.
PHMY 859.subject: PHMY
PHMY 859.title: Design and Conduct of Clinical Research Studies

PHMY 860.description: Case-based discussions that integrate and demonstrate applicability of other course material in patient care.
PHMY 860.subject: PHMY
PHMY 860.title: Clinical Applications V

PHMY 861.description: A capstone course, where case studies of complex patients and additional application exercises will bring together concepts learned throughout the previous semesters in the professional program.
PHMY 861.subject: PHMY
PHMY 861.title: Clinical Applications VI

PHMY 862.description: This course will primarily be a case-based class designed to enhance basic pharmaceutical science principles in which students clinically apply knowledge learned from current and past coursework in the University of South Carolina College of Pharmacy curriculum. Students will be required to develop assessments and plans for provided cases. SOAP notes will be required as specified. Each case will be fully discussed in each class period to enhance understanding of the topic. In addition to case-based discussions, students will be introduced to clinical practice exercises, including but not limited to a formulary review assignment, in preparation for the transition to Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experiences (APPEs) following the third professional year. Finally, students will be required to engage in peer evaluations throughout the course.
PHMY 862.subject: PHMY
PHMY 862.title: Patient Care Integration

PHMY 863.description: This course is designed to teach students proper medication safety practices. As medications are prescribed, prepared, dispensed and administered safely and appropriately, patients’ lives are ultimately improved. However, health care providers are human and thereby fallible by nature. Knowledge of ways in which medication errors commonly occur and the modalities in place to prevent such errors is important to the practice of pharmacy. This course will allow students to learn the history of medication safety, institutional policies, and technological advances in medication safety.
PHMY 863.subject: PHMY
PHMY 863.title: Medication Safety Management

PHMY 864.description: This course is a capstone course that will primarily be an application of current and past coursework in the College of Pharmacy curriculum to enhance knowledge learned and prepare students for Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experiences (APPEs). Assignments, presentations, exams, and patient cases will allow students to apply previously learned knowledge and demonstrate mastery of skills. Students will be required to work both individually and in groups to complete course assignments.
PHMY 864.subject: PHMY
PHMY 864.title: Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience Readiness

PHMY 873.description: This course is the third in a 4-semester sequence of courses providing a systems-based approach to pharmaceutical care and disease management. Students will learn about disease prevention and health promotion, as well as the drug and non-drug therapy of acute and chronic diseases seen in both hospitalized and ambulatory patients. Emphasis is placed on preventing, identifying, and solving drug-related problems. This course is coordinated with PHMY 822 , Pathophysiology and Pharmacology III.
PHMY 873.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PHMY 772, PHMY 773; third professional year standing.
PHMY 873.subject: PHMY
PHMY 873.title: Pharmacotherapy III

PHMY 874.description: This course is the fourth in a 4-semester sequence of courses providing a systems-based approach to pharmaceutical care and disease management. Students will learn about disease prevention and health promotion, as well as the drug and non-drug therapy of acute and chronic diseases seen in both hospitalized and ambulatory patients. Emphasis is placed on preventing, identifying, and solving drug-related problems. This course is coordinated with PHMY 823 , Pathophysiology and Pharmacology IV.
PHMY 874.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PHMY 873; third professional year standing.
PHMY 874.subject: PHMY
PHMY 874.title: Pharmacotherapy IV

PHMY 879.description: This elective prepares students to care for patients participating in medication therapy management. The focus will be on communicating with a patient during a MTM session to identify the patient’s current medication therapy problems and prevent future medication therapy problems. Students will apply therapeutic principles learned in the curriculum to improve the patient’s overall care, as related to the patient’s medication therapies.
PHMY 879.subject: PHMY
PHMY 879.title: Patient-Centered Approach to Medication Therapy Management

PHMY 880.description: This course is designed to provide students with advanced drug information practice and critical literature evaluation skills. This course provides students with the requisite skills to facilitate life-long learning.
PHMY 880.subject: PHMY
PHMY 880.title: Advanced Drug Information

PHMY 881.description: This course will introduce students to various topics related to the care of older patients in any setting. Course content will complement the PHMY curriculum in regard to geriatric pathophysiology, pharmacology, socioeconomics, regulations, and pharmacotherapeutics. In addition, it will expand upon the various practices of senior care pharmacy. Practicing consultants and other topic experts will serve as lecturers. In addition to class discussions and lectures, students will participate in a consultant pharmacist shadowing experience and will conduct an interview with a senior patient.
PHMY 881.subject: PHMY
PHMY 881.title: Senior Care Pharmacy Practice

PHMY 882.description: This course is an integrated approach to infectious diseases pharmacotherapy that builds upon required PHMY courses. At the conclusion of the course, the student will have a working knowledge of infectious diseases pharmacotherapy and be able to develop a complete patient care plan given an infectious diagnosis. Additionally, the course will stress important drug interactions with antimicrobials, adverse events associated with antimicrobials, and the prominent role of pharmacists in a HIV clinic, antimicrobial stewardship program, and/or medical crisis.
PHMY 882.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: second or third professional year standing.
PHMY 882.subject: PHMY
PHMY 882.title: Integrated Pharmacy: Infectious Diseases Pharmacotherapy in Patient Care

PHMY 884.description: This course will utilize the “Delivering MTM Services in the Community” certificate training program developed by APhA and ASCP to provide students the essential skills necessary to become a successful MTM practitioner. Students will learn how to evaluate complicated medication regimens, identify medication-related problems, and make recommendations. Aspects of business development and management will also be discussed. Students will participate in interactive lectures, reading and writing assignments, critical thinking exercises, and patient counseling sessions.
PHMY 884.subject: PHMY
PHMY 884.title: Delivering MTM Services

PHMY 885.description: This course offers an in-depth exploration of federal and state laws and regulations that guide and regulate the practice of pharmacy. It covers the critical legal frameworks pharmacists must apply to ensure compliance and to maintain professional standards. The course also introduces essential professional and ethical issues relevant to pharmacy practice, highlighting their importance in protecting patient safety and sustaining public trust.
PHMY 885.subject: PHMY
PHMY 885.title: Pharmacy Law and Ethics

PHMY 886.description: This challenging course is designed to provide the student with the opportunity to gather, analyze, and synthesize medical information from complex patient cases into complete pharmacotherapeutic treatment plans designed to improve patient outcomes. This process will enhance the student’s ability to be an independent and active learner, foster the student’s individual and group problem solving abilities, promote the critical examination of medical problems, and develop student’s clinical skills and decision-making abilities.
PHMY 886.subject: PHMY
PHMY 886.title: Pharmacotherapy Cases

PHMY 887.description: This elective course is designed to provide the student with increased exposure to disease states and medications in the specialty of endocrinology. In addition, the student will have the opportunity to refine clinical knowledge, decision-making skills, and presentation ability within this course. This course will provide active learning opportunities involving clinical debates, drug information questions, and disease state presentations.
PHMY 887.subject: PHMY
PHMY 887.title: Advanced Endocrinology

PHMY 890.description: Clinical application of basic pharmacokinetic principles to safe and effective patient management with emphasis on design of dosage regimens, therapeutic monitoring, and adjustment of therapy. Application illustrated and practiced through discussions and case examples.
PHMY 890.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PHMY 710; second professional year standing.
PHMY 890.subject: PHMY
PHMY 890.title: Clinical Pharmacokinetics

PHMY 891.description: This course will incorporate didactic teaching from both the basic sciences and pharmacotherapy realms to prepare students to effectively engage with commonly encountered questions and pharmacy practice dilemmas related to pharmacogenomics. The course will also provide active learning through longitudinal projects involving pharmacogenomic literature analysis, and solving pharmacogenetics-related pharmacotherapy selection problems.
PHMY 891.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: second or third professional year standing.
PHMY 891.subject: PHMY
PHMY 891.title: Clinical Pharmacogenomics and Advanced Personalized Medicine

PHMY 895.description: Development of clinical assessment skills necessary in the provision of pharmaceutical care to patients with a variety of disease states.
PHMY 895.subject: PHMY
PHMY 895.title: Clinical Assessment

PHMY 898.description: The objective of this course is to introduce nursing, pharmacy and social work students to direct telemental health practice in health settings – the use of telecommunications technology to provide behavioral health sciences. This course provides health professions students with a detailed examination of the use of telehealth processes to transform the provision of healthcare. Through an interprofessional context, students will learn the history and status of telemental health activities; engage with stimulated and live telemental health learning experiences; understand the use of telemental health to improve healthcare access and population health; and embrace the changing models of care resulting from advancing telemental health technologies.
PHMY 898.subject: PHMY
PHMY 898.title: Telemental Health

PHMY 963.description: This required advanced pharmacy practice experience (APPE) provides clinical pharmacy activity on a variety of adult and pediatric medicine inpatient services including cardiology, critical care, emergency medicine, geriatrics, gastrointestinal, infectious disease, nephrology, OB-GYN, oncology, psychiatry, pulmonary and transplant. The APPE provides an exposure to a variety of disease states that allows the student to gain experience monitoring drug therapy and to participate in the therapeutic decision making process. Additional competencies to be achieved during this APPE include: (1) how to develop a problem list, (2) how to present a patient, (3) how to develop and implement a monitoring plan, (4) how to take a medication history, (5) how to respond to a drug information request, and (6) review the policies and procedures at the institution.
PHMY 963.subject: PHMY
PHMY 963.title: Acute/General Medicine Pharmacy Practice Experience I

PHMY 970.description: This required advanced pharmacy practice experience (APPE) involves the student in the daily provision of clinical pharmacy services in the ambulatory care setting including anticoagulation, geriatrics, HIV, Indian Health Services, oncology, pain management, and primary care. Responsibilities include providing drug therapy for disease states commonly encountered in the outpatient setting, providing drug regimen reviews, physical assessment and interviewing patients to elicit drug histories, health status, and adherence to therapy. A significant aspect of this rotation pertains to the long-term management of chronically ill patients.
PHMY 970.subject: PHMY
PHMY 970.title: Ambulatory Care Pharmacy Practice Experience I

PHMY 983.description: Elective pharmacy practice experiences provide students with the opportunity to explore a variety of pharmacy practice settings outside of the four core curricular categories (acute/general medicine, ambulatory care, community, and hospital/health system). These elective experiences are typically in non-traditional pharmacy settings and include, but are not limited to, academia, administration, drug information, industry, informatics, international, investigational drug services, long term care, mail order, managed care, nuclear, poison center, research and veterinary medicine.

A follow-up question and answer period examines the student’s ability to substantiate his/her conclusions. Content and presentation technique will be critiqued.
